newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Shooting breaks out at Sierra Leone airport.
newsitem.headline: Shooting breaks out at Sierra Leone airport.

text.p: Shelling or mortar fire broke out at the international airport in Sierra Leone's capital Freetown on Wednesday but it was not immediately clear who was firing at whom, residents and military sources said.

Nigerian troops, members of a force that has been strengthened as part of efforts to reinstate ousted President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, are stationed at the airport which is across an estuary from the capital itself.

Soldiers at strategic positions in the city, where junior army officers seized power on May 25, told Reuters that Nigerian troops had opened fire to stop some Sierra Leone troops who tried to make their way to the airport.

The sound of the firing caused panic in the centre of Freetown, which has been jittery since Tuesday when a clandestine broadcast by Kabbah stoked fear of another attack by Nigeria. Nigerian gunboats bombarded Freetown on June 2 in a show of force.

Sierra Leone's West African neighbours resolved on June 26 at a meeting of their foreign ministers in Conakry, capital of neighbouring Guinea, to press for Kabbah's return to power by dialogue and economic sanctions initially, but retained the option using force.
